decisive_items: a large, well-circumscribed, expansile, heterogeneous (mixed-density) mass occupying the entire left maxillary sinus
deviation and destruction of the nasal septum, invaded the ethmoid sinus, thinned, displaced, and perforated the anterior wall of the sphenoid sinus
response.rationale: The champion candidate, R2, is supported by the presence of a large, expansile mass in the maxillary sinus with invasion into surrounding structures, which is consistent with juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma. The runner-up candidate, C1, is also a type of angiofibroma, but it is more specific to the left maxillary sinus. The decisive items highlight the aggressive nature of the tumor, which is more consistent with juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma. The counterfactual missing items include the lack of family history of cherubism, bilateral involvement of the maxilla, and histopathological features of odontogenic myxoma, which are not present in the vignette and make the other candidates less likely.

rejected.why: lack of specific features of fibrous dysplasia, such as ground-glass appearance on radiographs
lack of bilateral involvement and family history of cherubism
lack of specific features of odontogenic myxoma, such as histopathological features and characteristic radiographic appearance
